why: A earns its advantage on the three criteria that matter most for a scholar deciding what Riley's engagement amounts to: fidelity checking against the actual Weber pages, specificity about which attributions hold and which do not, and coherent identification of tensions within Riley's own corpus. A checks twenty-eight citation pairs and distinguishes accurate verbatim matches (E&S p. 919, pp. 1028-31, p. 53) from selective enlargements (political-society formula, capitalism-suffrage thesis, tax-farming genealogy) and one material substitution (the census article's state definition, where bureaucratic-infrastructural capacity is attributed to pages that define the state by monopoly of legitimate physical force). These distinctions are grounded in the held Weber primary windows that appear in the source packet. A also identifies and names an unresolved internal tension in Riley's corpus—the 2018 rejection of estate concepts for advanced capitalism versus the 2025 application of those same concepts to political capitalism—and states clearly that the supplied texts do not reconcile it. B does none of this. B's fidelity treatment is almost entirely absent: it notes that Riley adapts or credits Weber but never checks whether the cited pages establish what Riley claims. B uses the Weber passage at E&S p. 919 without verifying it; it accepts the state definition in the census article without noting the substitution; it does not flag the political-society formula problem. B's reception section situates Riley among other readers by function (genealogy, foil, authority) rather than by analytical consonance and contrast on specific fault lines. The observation about the internal estate-politics tension does not appear in B at all. A's claim that Riley's 2026 'Angles of Vision' performs an epistemological Einkesselung of Weber rather than a simple adoption is a non-obvious interpretive finding that B misses. B is accurate in its inventory of where Weber appears and competent in characterizing the move type, but it operates at a lower analytical resolution throughout.
what_A_has_that_B_lacks: Checked fidelity verdicts keyed to specific Weber page predicates (the state-definition substitution at pp. 77-78, the verbatim match at p. 919, the two-predicate confirmation at pp. 1028-31, the word-for-word match at p. 53); explicit identification and naming of the unresolved 2018/2025 estate-politics tension within Riley's own corpus; a structured reception comparison that positions Riley against Wright, Ganev, Ktenas, Bendix, and Love on three specific fault lines (estate reinforcement vs. erosion, state weakness vs. state capacity in political capitalism, historicist critique vs. defence of Wertfreiheit); the 'selective enlargement vs. accurate narrow quotation' pattern as a precise diagnostic framework rather than a general observation; the Lukácsian Einkesselung reading of the 2026 text as Riley's most metatheoretically explicit move.
what_B_has_that_A_lacks: A cleaner text-by-text inventory organized by document with the Riley quote given for each passage, which makes it easier to trace which passage in which text corresponds to which Weber use; the biographical footnote on 'Social Causes of the Decline of Ancient Civilization' as Riley's vocational origin, which A does not register; slightly crisper prose on what Riley does not engage in Weber (the comparative world-religions work, the ancient history, the correspondence).
